title: Global patterns and driving factors of non-leaf litter carbon quality across plant functional types and environments
content:
Abstract
Carbon (C) quality of non-leaf litter, namely bark, branch, flower, fruit, root, stem, and wood, closely relates to decomposition rate and plays a vital role in the sequestration of terrestrial ecosystem C. However, to date, the global patterns and driving factors of the C quality of non-leaf litter remain unclear. Here, using meta-analysis, we estimated the initial C quality of non-leaf litter, including indices of the concentrations of total C, lignin, cellulose, and hemicellulose and analyzed their driving factors. Our results showed that (1) only total C and cellulose concentrations significantly varied among different types of non-leaf litter; (2) C quality is higher (i.e. lower concentration) in bark, branch, root, stem and wood litter of angiosperms than gymnosperms, of herbaceous than woody plants, of broadleaved than coniferous trees, and of arbuscular mycorrhizal plants than ectomycorrhizal plants (except for hemicellulose concentration); and (3) the impacts of different geographic parameters on C quality of non-leaf litter differed among different litter types, while soil properties generally showed strong impacts. Overall, our results show the global patterns of C quality and driving factors for different types of non-leaf litter, which would be helpful for a better understanding of the role of non-leaf litter in the terrestrial ecosystem C cycling and for the improvement of C cycling models.
